decisions: Phase 6 solves only supported direct recursion with semantic self-call identity, compatible base-case evidence, proven reducing arguments, path-aware recursive-call multiplicity, and known non-recursive local work.
Recurrence extraction and recurrence solving remain separate internal responsibilities under analyzer/src/ComplexityAnalysis.Analyzers/Analysis/Recursion/.
The recurrence model is internal to the isolated analyzer and independent from inherited solver/core projects.

Supported solver families are summation/decrement, simple constant-coefficient exponential recurrences including Fibonacci-like order-2 forms, Master Theorem for one scaled recursive term, and restricted/bounded Akra-Bazzi for scale-only unequal splits.
Fractional polynomial powers and exponential bases use deterministic invariant formatting with bounded normalization.
Unsupported, invalid, numerically inconclusive, unknown-local-work, missing-base-case, non-reducing, and mutual-recursive cases remain Unknown.
BIG0001 reports solved recursive estimates only when enabled; BIG1005 reports only solved exponential direct-recursive growth.
constraints: Do not modify inherited projects outside analyzer/.
Do not create ProjectReference, binary reference, local package dependency, or transitive dependency on inherited projects.
Do not add MathNet.Numerics, SymPy, Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces, or Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces.
Do not claim full Akra-Bazzi, general symbolic recurrence solving, mutual recursion solving, memoization detection, or whole-compilation recurrence scanning.
validations: All Phase 6 acceptance criteria were checked against code, tests, diagnostics, documentation, dependency audit, package inspection, and upstream isolation.

Recurrence extraction audit covered direct recursion semantic identity, base-case evidence, reducing arguments, branch-exclusive calls, sequential multiplicity, local-work extraction, and mutual recursion boundaries.

Solver matrix covered summation/decrement, simple exponential recurrence, Fibonacci-like recurrence, Master Theorem cases 1/2/3, fractional Master exponent, restricted Akra-Bazzi unequal split, unsupported recurrence, and numerical inconclusiveness.
False-positive audit confirmed missing base case, non-reducing recursion, mutual recursion, unsupported recurrence, numerical inconclusive result, and unknown local work remain Unknown.

Diagnostic audit confirmed BIG0001/BIG1001/BIG1002/BIG1003/BIG1004/BIG1005/BIG9000 alignment across SupportedDiagnostics, DiagnosticDescriptors, AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md, docs/en/analyzers.md, and docs/pt-BR/analyzers.md.
Dependency audit found no MathNet.Numerics, SymPy, Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces, Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces, or inherited ProjectReference in the analyzer product.
Analyzer validation passed: dotnet restore; dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore; dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build with 472 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
Local Release package 0.6.0-phase6-validation was inspected: analyzer DLL under analyzers/dotnet/cs, README.md included, no lib assets, no dependency groups, and no forbidden assemblies.

Upstream isolation was confirmed: no files outside analyzer/ differ from the initial HEAD; root restore/build passed with an isolated NuGet cache and redirected MkDocs output after the default environment hit a corrupt global NuGet metadata file and a docs/api file lock.
